description: 32 gold contract audit cases covering all domains including Bengali Property Sale (LSA-2026-002) and Full Software Development Agreement (SDA-2026-011) with Playbook enforcement. v1.1.0: added 4 full-length contracts (3 compliant LOW baselines + 1 HIGH statutory-trap supply contract) for full-pipeline and false-positive coverage. v1.1.0: added 4 full-length contracts (3 compliant LOW baselines + 1 HIGH statutory-trap supply contract) for full-pipeline and false-positive coverage.

cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 6: NON-COMPETE
Upon termination or resignation for any reason, Employee shall not join, consult for, or establish any competing software or IT business anywhere in Bangladesh for a period of three (3) years.
cases.notes: Post-employment non-compete is VOID_AB_INITIO under Contract Act s.27.

cases.contract_title: At-Will Instant Termination Clause
cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 3: TERMINATION
The Employer reserves the absolute right to terminate the permanent Employee at any time with immediate effect without assigning any reason, without prior notice, and without any severance or notice pay.
cases.notes: Violates Bangladesh Labour Act 2006 Section 26 (120/60 days notice or pay in lieu + 30 days/year compensation).

cases.contract_title: Compliant Permanent Employment Agreement
cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 1: APPOINTMENT AND PROBATION
Employee is appointed as Senior Operations Manager subject to a 3-month probation period.

CLAUSE 2: TERMINATION AND SEVERANCE
After confirmation as a permanent monthly-rated employee, Employer may terminate employment by giving 120 days prior written notice or wages in lieu thereof, together with statutory compensation of 30 days wages for each completed year of service or gratuity, whichever is higher, in accordance with Section 26 of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.

CLAUSE 3: PROVIDENT FUND AND GRATUITY
Employee shall be entitled to statutory provident fund and gratuity benefits upon separation.

CLAUSE 4: CONFIDENTIALITY
During and after employment, Employee shall not disclose proprietary trade secrets or confidential client lists of the Employer. Nothing herein restricts lawful future employment.
cases.notes: Compliant baseline employment contract — tests low false-positive rate.

cases.contract_title: Training Bond & Certificate Retention
cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 5: MINIMUM SERVICE BOND
Employee agrees to serve the Company for a mandatory lock-in period of 4 years. If Employee resigns early, Employee shall forfeit all unpaid salary and pay BDT 10,00,000 as fixed liquidated penalty regardless of actual training cost.

CLAUSE 6: ORIGINAL DOCUMENTS
Company shall retain Employee's original university degree certificates and NID card in custody until completion of the 4-year bond.
cases.notes: Tests Section 74 penalty moderation + illegal retention of original documents / restraint.

cases.contract_title: SaaS Vendor-Favorable IP & Advance Forfeiture
cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 1: SCOPE AND ADVANCE PAYMENT
Client shall pay BDT 20,00,000 (50% advance) on signing. All advance payments are strictly non-refundable under all circumstances, including Vendor's early termination or non-delivery.

CLAUSE 2: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
Vendor retains exclusive worldwide copyright and source code ownership of all custom software developed under this Agreement. Client receives only a revocable annual license.

CLAUSE 3: ACCEPTANCE TESTING
Deliverables shall be deemed irrevocably accepted if Client fails to submit written defect reports within 48 hours of staging upload.

CLAUSE 4: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
Vendor's total liability for data breaches, gross negligence, or willful misconduct shall not exceed BDT 10,000.
cases.notes: Multi-clause Tech SaaS audit protecting Client.

cases.contract_title: Client-Favorable Unlimited Liability & IP Pre-Payment Trap
cases.contract_text:
CUSTOM SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT
CLAUSE 1: PAYMENT
Client will pay invoices within 120 days of final go-live sign-off at Client's sole subjective satisfaction.

CLAUSE 2: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
All pre-existing Vendor frameworks, libraries, and future know-how become Client's exclusive property upon signing, even prior to payment.

CLAUSE 3: INDEMNITY AND LIABILITY
Vendor assumes unlimited liability for any indirect, consequential, or lost-profit damages suffered by Client, with no liability cap.

CLAUSE 4: CHANGE REQUESTS
Vendor shall implement any additional features requested by Client during the project at zero additional fee.
cases.notes: Perspective flip test: audited_for=VENDOR must protect Vendor against unlimited liability, scope creep, and pre-payment IP loss.

cases.contract_title: Compliant Balanced Software Development Agreement
cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 1: DELIVERABLES AND ACCEPTANCE
Vendor shall deliver custom software modules per Appendix A. Client shall have 15 business days for User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Vendor shall fix defects within 10 business days.

CLAUSE 2: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT
Upon full payment of milestone fees, Vendor hereby assigns all copyright and source code ownership of custom deliverables to Client in writing pursuant to Copyright Act, 2000 (Sections 15, 17). Vendor warrants no copyleft Open Source Software (GPL) is embedded without Client's written approval.

CLAUSE 3: DATA SECURITY AND BREACH NOTIFICATION
Vendor shall maintain encryption and notify Client within 48 hours of any data security breach in compliance with the Cyber Security Act, 2023.

CLAUSE 4: TERMINATION AND REFUND
Upon termination for Vendor breach, Vendor shall refund all unearned advance payments for unperformed services within 15 days under Sections 64 and 65 of The Contract Act, 1872.

CLAUSE 5: IP INDEMNIFICATION & DISPUTE RESOLUTION
Vendor indemnifies Client against third-party IP infringement claims. Disputes shall be resolved by arbitration seated in Dhaka under the Arbitration Act, 2001.
cases.notes: Compliant baseline SaaS agreement — should NOT falsely flag HIGH risks.

cases.contract_title: Enterprise Playbook Enforcement Test

ENTERPRISE SAAS SERVICES AGREEMENT
CLAUSE 1: PAYMENT TERMS
Client shall pay 100% of annual fee upfront. Invoices are net-7.

CLAUSE 2: LIABILITY CAP

playbook_rules.rule_description: Enterprise policy prohibits 100% upfront payment; maximum allowable advance is 30% with minimum Net-30 invoice terms.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Client shall pay 30% mobilization advance and remaining 70% on milestone delivery within Net-30 days.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Vendor aggregate liability cap must be at least 12 months of contract fees.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Vendor's aggregate liability shall be capped at 100% of total fees paid in the preceding 12 months.

cases.notes: Tests Enterprise Company Playbook Rule ID citation enforcement.

cases.contract_title: Long MSA Needle-in-a-Haystack Risk Test (~9,000 chars)
cases.contract_text:
MASTER SOFTWARE SERVICES AGREEMENT

CLAUSE 1: DEFINITIONS
1.1 'Affiliate' means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where control means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of voting securities.
1.2 'Business Day' means any day other than a Friday, Saturday, or gazetted public holiday declared by the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in Dhaka.
1.3 'Confidential Information' means all non-public technical, financial, commercial, architectural, and customer data disclosed by either Party in written, oral, or electronic form.
1.4 'Deliverables' means the software code, technical documentation, API specifications, and deployment scripts set forth in an executed Statement of Work.
1.5 'Documentation' means user manuals, system administration guides, and API reference sheets provided by Vendor in English.

CLAUSE 2: GOVERNANCE AND SERVICE LEVELS
2.1 Vendor shall assign a dedicated Project Manager who shall conduct weekly sprint review calls with Client's designated Product Owner.
2.2 Production services hosted under this Agreement shall maintain 99.9% monthly uptime availability excluding scheduled maintenance windows announced 72 hours in advance.
2.3 Service credits for uptime shortfall below 99.9% shall be applied against the subsequent quarterly invoice in accordance with Schedule B.
2.4 Vendor shall maintain automated daily encrypted backups stored across redundant availability zones with a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 4 hours and Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 8 hours.

CLAUSE 3: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT
3.1 Upon full payment of the applicable milestone invoice, Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Client all right, title, and interest, including worldwide copyright and source code ownership, in all custom Deliverables created specifically for Client pursuant to the Copyright Act, 2000.
3.2 Vendor represents and warrants that no GPL or copyleft Open Source Software requiring source disclosure will be embedded in Deliverables without Client's prior written consent.
3.3 Vendor shall defend and indemnify Client against any third-party claim alleging that Deliverables infringe a valid patent or copyright.

CLAUSE 4: DATA SECURITY AND INCIDENT NOTIFICATION
4.1 Vendor shall implement industry-standard encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit), role-based access controls, and annual penetration testing.
4.2 In the event of any confirmed or suspected unauthorized access or personal data breach, Vendor shall notify Client in writing within 48 hours and cooperate fully with remediation under the Cyber Security Act, 2023.
4.3 Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor without Client's prior written authorization.

CLAUSE 5: ACCEPTANCE TESTING
5.1 Client shall have fifteen (15) Business Days following delivery of each milestone to perform User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
5.2 If Client identifies material non-conformities, Vendor shall cure such defects at no additional charge within ten (10) Business Days.

CLAUSE 6: AUDIT RIGHTS AND COMPLIANCE
6.1 During the term and for one (1) year thereafter, Client or its independent auditor may inspect relevant security and billing records upon 15 days notice during regular business hours.
6.2 Both Parties shall comply with applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and tax withholding laws of Bangladesh.

CLAUSE 7: SPECIAL RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES
7.1 Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, upon termination or expiry of this Agreement for any reason, Client and its key engineering personnel shall be prohibited from developing, procuring, or operating any competing retail analytics platform anywhere in Bangladesh for a period of five (5) years. Furthermore, if Client delays any invoice payment by more than three (3) days, Client shall pay a non-negotiable compounding penalty of 10% per month (120% per annum) and Vendor shall retain all advance deposits paid by Client even if Vendor terminates for convenience without delivering remaining milestones.

CLAUSE 8: INSURANCE
8.1 Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability and cyber liability insurance policies with reputable insurers licensed in Bangladesh throughout the Term.
8.2 Vendor shall furnish certificates of insurance within 14 days of Client's written request.

CLAUSE 9: FORCE MAJEURE
9.1 Neither Party shall be liable for failure to perform due to unforeseeable events beyond reasonable control such as floods, earthquakes, war, or nationwide telecommunications shutdowns, provided written notice is given within 72 hours.
9.2 Normal inflation, currency fluctuation, or supplier pricing increases shall not constitute a Force Majeure event.

CLAUSE 10: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
10.1 Each Party represents that it is duly incorporated and validly existing under the laws of Bangladesh and has full corporate authority to execute this Agreement.
10.2 Vendor warrants that Deliverables will substantially conform to specifications for 90 days post-acceptance and will be free from malicious code or backdoors.

CLAUSE 11: NOTICES
11.1 All formal notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand with acknowledgement or by registered post with A/D to the registered office addresses in Dhaka specified on the signature page, with courtesy copy by email.

CLAUSE 12: DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW
12.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.
12.2 Any dispute not amicably settled within 30 days shall be referred to binding domestic arbitration seated in Dhaka in accordance with the Arbitration Act, 2001 before a sole arbitrator mutually appointed by the Parties.

CLAUSE 13: MISCELLANEOUS
13.1 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes prior negotiations.
13.2 Amendments require a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.
13.3 Failure to enforce any right shall not operate as a waiver thereof.
cases.notes: Long-context Needle-in-a-Haystack test: Clauses 1-6 and 8-13 are clean/compliant, but Clause 7 buries 3 severe Bangladesh statutory violations (s.27 non-compete, s.74 120% penalty, s.65 advance forfeiture).

cases.contract_title: Unregistered 5-Year Commercial Lease on Plain Paper
cases.contract_text:
CLAUSE 1: TERM AND EXECUTION
Landlord hereby leases the 4,000 sq. ft. commercial office space in Gulshan-2, Dhaka to Tenant for a fixed term of five (5) years at BDT 3,50,000 per month. This lease deed is executed exclusively on plain A4 paper and shall not be registered at the Sub-Registry Office.

All information shared by Disclosing Party, including information already in the public domain or independently developed by Receiving Party, is permanently confidential.

CLAUSE 2: TERM

cases.contract_title: Long Employment Contract with Buried Unlawful Deductions (~7,500 chars)
cases.contract_text:
EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

CLAUSE 1: POSITION AND WORKPLACE
1.1 Employer hereby engages Employee as Senior Finance Analyst at its Dhaka Corporate Office.
1.2 Standard working hours shall be Sunday through Thursday, 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, with statutory weekly holidays and festival leaves under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.

CLAUSE 2: REMUNERATION AND BENEFITS
2.1 Employee shall receive a gross monthly salary of BDT 95,000 payable on or before the 5th working day of the following month via bank transfer.
2.2 Employee shall be entitled to annual festival bonuses equivalent to two basic salaries and contributory provident fund after confirmation.
2.3 Gratuity shall be payable upon separation in accordance with statutory thresholds.

CLAUSE 3: LEAVE ENTITLEMENTS
3.1 Employee shall be entitled to 10 days casual leave, 14 days sick leave with medical certificate, and annual earned leave as prescribed by Chapter IX of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
3.2 Unavailed earned leave shall be encashed upon termination or retirement.

CLAUSE 4: CODE OF CONDUCT AND SAFETY
4.1 Employer maintains a zero-tolerance policy against workplace harassment and ensures safe working conditions.
4.2 Employee shall comply with published IT acceptable use and expense reimbursement guidelines.

CLAUSE 5: CONFIDENTIALITY DURING EMPLOYMENT
5.1 Employee shall safeguard proprietary financial models, client account records, and pricing matrices during employment and thereafter.

CLAUSE 6: SPECIAL SEPARATION, DEDUCTION AND NON-COMPETE TERMS
6.1 Regardless of tenure, if Employer terminates Employee for business restructuring, Employer shall give only 7 days notice with zero statutory severance or compensation. Furthermore, upon any separation, Employee is barred from working in any accounting, audit, or finance role anywhere in Bangladesh for 3 years, and Employer may unilaterally deduct 50% of Employee's final salary as an administrative separation fee.

CLAUSE 7: GOVERNING LAW
7.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of Bangladesh, including the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
cases.notes: Long employment contract with buried violations in Clause 6.

cases.contract_title: জমি ক্রয়-বিক্রয় চুক্তিপত্র (LSA-2026-002 - Real Bengali PDF Sample)
cases.contract_text:
জমি ক্রয়-বিক্রয় চুক্তিপত্র
(AGREEMENT FOR SALE OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY)
দলিল রেফারেন্স: LSA-2026-002
চুক্তির তারিখ: ১২ নভেম্বর ২০২৬
চুক্তি সম্পাদনের স্থান: সাভার, ঢাকা, বাংলাদেশ।

১. চুক্তির পক্ষসমূহ
প্রথম পক্ষ – বিক্রেতা
নাম: মোঃ আব্দুল করিম, পিতার নাম: মোঃ আব্দুল হাকিম, ঠিকানা: গ্রাম: রাজাশন, ডাকঘর: সাভার, উপজেলা: সাভার, জেলা: ঢাকা।
দ্বিতীয় পক্ষ – ক্রেতা
নাম: মোঃ সাইফুল ইসলাম, পিতার নাম: মোঃ আব্দুল জলিল, ঠিকানা: গ্রাম: আমিনবাজার, উপজেলা: সাভার, জেলা: ঢাকা।

২. জমির তফসিল
জেলা: ঢাকা, উপজেলা: সাভার, মৌজা: রাজাশন, জে.এল. নম্বর: ৪৫, সাব-রেজিস্ট্রি অফিস: সাভার, সি.এস. খতিয়ান: ১২০, এস.এ. খতিয়ান: ১৮৫, আর.এস. খতিয়ান: ৩১০, বি.এস. খতিয়ান: ৫২৫, দাগ নম্বর: ১২৩৪, জমির পরিমাণ: ১০ (দশ) শতাংশ, জমির শ্রেণি: ভিটা।

৩. মালিকানার বিবরণ
বিক্রেতার দাবি অনুযায়ী, উক্ত জমি তাঁর পিতা মোঃ আব্দুল হাকিম ১৯৯৮ সালে রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত দলিল নং ১২৫৬/১৯৯৮ মাধ্যমে ক্রয় করেন। পিতার মৃত্যুর পর বিক্রেতা উত্তরাধিকারসূত্রে জমিটির মালিকানা লাভ করেন। বিক্রেতা জানান, তাঁর আরও দুইজন ভাই ও একজন বোন রয়েছেন। তবে তাঁদের সম্মতি বা অনাপত্তিপত্র গ্রহণের প্রয়োজন নেই, কারণ জমিটি বর্তমানে তাঁর দখলে রয়েছে। বিক্রেতা আরও দাবি করেন যে, জমিটির সম্পূর্ণ মালিকানা তাঁর নিজের।

৪. বিক্রয়মূল্য ও অর্থ পরিশোধ
উক্ত ১০ শতাংশ জমির মোট বিক্রয়মূল্য ২৫,০০,০০০ (পঁচিশ লক্ষ) টাকা। ক্রেতা চুক্তি স্বাক্ষরের সময় অগ্রিম ৫,০০,০০০ টাকা, দলিল রেজিস্ট্রেশনের আগে ১৫,০০,০০০ টাকা এবং জমির দখল বুঝে নেওয়ার সময় ৫,০০,০০০ টাকা পরিশোধ করবেন। বিক্রেতা ইতোমধ্যে ৫,০০,০০০ টাকা গ্রহণ করেছেন।

৫. জমির দায়-দেনা ও বন্ধক
বিক্রেতা ঘোষণা করছেন যে জমিটি কোনো ব্যাংক বা আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের কাছে বন্ধক রাখা হয়নি। তবে জমির পূর্ববর্তী মালিকের কোনো ঋণ বা দায় থাকলে বিক্রেতা তার দায়ভার গ্রহণ করবেন না। জমির বিরুদ্ধে কোনো মামলা বা আইনি বিরোধ থাকলে ক্রেতা নিজ দায়িত্বে তা নিষ্পত্তি করবেন।

৬. নামজারি ও খাজনা
বিক্রেতা জানান যে জমিটির সর্বশেষ নামজারি তাঁর পিতা মোঃ আব্দুল হাকিমের নামে রয়েছে (খতিয়ান ৫২৫)। বিক্রেতার নামে নতুন নামজারি সম্পন্ন হয়নি। বিক্রেতা দাবি করেন, নামজারি না থাকলেও জমিটি বিক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে কোনো বাধা নেই।

৭. জমির দখল হস্তান্তর
দলিল রেজিস্ট্রেশনের দিন বিক্রেতা জমির দখল ক্রেতাকে বুঝিয়ে দেবেন। জমির একাংশ বর্তমানে স্থানীয় একজন ব্যক্তি ব্যবহার করছেন। ক্রেতা জমির বাস্তব দখল যাচাই না করেই চুক্তিতে সম্মত হয়েছেন।

৮. পূর্ববর্তী বিক্রয় ও তৃতীয় পক্ষের অধিকার
জমির একটি অংশ নিয়ে পূর্বে অন্য একজন ব্যক্তির সঙ্গে মৌখিক বায়না চুক্তি হয়েছিল। এ বিষয়ে কোনো লিখিত বাতিল চুক্তি বা অনাপত্তিপত্র সংযুক্ত করা হয়নি।

৯. দলিল রেজিস্ট্রেশন
উভয় পক্ষ আগামী ৩০ দিনের মধ্যে সাফ কবলা দলিল রেজিস্ট্রেশন সম্পন্ন করবেন। বিক্রেতা নির্ধারিত সময়ে রেজিস্ট্রেশন করতে ব্যর্থ হলে ক্রেতা অগ্রিম অর্থ ফেরত পাবেন। তবে অতিরিক্ত ক্ষতিপূরণ বা জরিমানার বিষয়ে কোনো শর্ত নির্ধারণ করা হয়নি।

১০. বিক্রেতার ঘোষণা ও নিশ্চয়তা
তবে উপরোক্ত ঘোষণাগুলোর পক্ষে কোনো স্বাধীন মালিকানা অনুসন্ধান প্রতিবেদন বা আইনজীবীর Title Search Report সংযুক্ত করা হয়নি।

১১. চুক্তি বাতিল
ক্রেতা কোনো কারণে জমি কিনতে অস্বীকৃতি জানালে বিক্রেতা অগ্রিম অর্থের ৫০% বাজেয়াপ্ত করতে পারবেন। বিক্রেতা জমি বিক্রি করতে অস্বীকৃতি জানালে ক্রেতাকে কেবল অগ্রিম অর্থ ফেরত দেওয়া হবে। কোনো পক্ষই অতিরিক্ত ক্ষতিপূরণ দাবি করতে পারবেন না।

১২. বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তি
আলোচনায় সমাধান না হলে উভয় পক্ষের সম্মতিতে সালিশের মাধ্যমে ঢাকায় বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তি করা হবে।

১৩. প্রযোজ্য আইন
Transfer of Property Act, 1882; Registration Act, 1908; Contract Act, 1872; State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950; Specific Relief Act, 1877।

cases.contract_title: Software Development & Technology Service Agreement (SDA-2026-011 + Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001)
cases.contract_text:
SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT & TECHNOLOGY SERVICE AGREEMENT
Agreement Reference: SDA-2026-011
Date of Execution: 12 November 2026
Place of Execution: Dhaka, Bangladesh

1. PARTIES TO THE AGREEMENT
Party A – Client: Nexora Digital Solutions Ltd., House 45, Road 12, Banani, Dhaka-1213, Bangladesh (Authorized Representative: Mr. Rahman Ahmed, Managing Director).
Party B – Service Provider: ByteCraft Technologies Ltd., Level 6, Sector 7, Uttara, Dhaka-1230, Bangladesh (Authorized Representative: Mr. Tanvir Hasan, Chief Executive Officer).

2. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF SERVICES
The Service Provider agrees to design, develop, deploy, and maintain a cloud-based Enterprise Resource Management (ERP) software platform for the Client. Any additional functionality requested by the Client shall be considered part of the original scope unless otherwise agreed in writing.

3. CONTRACT VALUE AND PAYMENT TERMS
The total contract value shall be BDT 12,00,000 (Twelve Lakh Bangladeshi Taka). The Client agrees to make payments according to the following schedule: 40% advance payment upon signing this Agreement; 30% upon completion of the development phase; 30% upon final delivery of the software. The Service Provider shall be entitled to demand additional payments for unexpected technical requirements. All payments must be completed within 15 business days of receiving an invoice. In case of delayed payment, the Client shall pay a late payment charge of 5% per day on the outstanding amount. The Service Provider may suspend services immediately if payment is delayed by more than 7 days.

4. PROJECT TIMELINE AND DELIVERY
The project shall commence on 15 November 2026 and be completed within 90 calendar days. Any delay caused by the Client shall automatically extend the delivery deadline. However, the Service Provider shall remain responsible for delivering the project within the originally agreed timeline. The Service Provider may change the delivery schedule without obtaining prior written approval from the Client.

5. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS
All software code, source files, databases, documentation, designs created under this Agreement shall belong exclusively to the Client immediately upon commencement of the project. The Client shall not be required to make the final payment before obtaining complete ownership of the software. The Service Provider may reuse any part of the developed software for other commercial clients without obtaining prior written permission from the Client.

6. CONFIDENTIALITY
Both parties agree to maintain confidentiality of business, financial, technical, customer, and credential information. Neither party shall disclose confidential information to any third party without prior written consent. This obligation shall remain valid for a period of two years following termination of this Agreement. The Service Provider shall not be responsible for unauthorized disclosure of information caused by its employees, subcontractors, or third-party service providers.

7. DATA PROTECTION AND SECURITY
The Service Provider shall implement reasonable security measures to protect the Client's data. The Service Provider may store, process, transfer, or share Client data with third-party hosting providers and external vendors whenever technically necessary. The Service Provider shall not be required to notify the Client immediately in the event of a data breach unless the Client specifically requests such notification. The Service Provider shall not be liable for any data loss resulting from third-party cloud infrastructure failures.

8. WARRANTIES AND MAINTENANCE
The Service Provider warrants that the delivered software will substantially comply with agreed technical specifications. A 30-day maintenance period shall begin after the initial deployment to correct defects without additional charges. Any modifications, performance improvements, security updates, or compatibility changes shall be considered additional paid services. The Service Provider does not guarantee uninterrupted availability or error-free operation.

9. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
The Service Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed BDT 50,000 under any circumstances. Neither party shall be responsible for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages. However, the Service Provider shall be responsible for all direct and indirect financial losses resulting from its negligence, misconduct, or failure to perform contractual obligations.

10. INDEMNIFICATION
The Service Provider agrees to indemnify the Client against all claims, damages, losses, expenses, and liabilities arising from development and delivery of the software. The Client shall also indemnify the Service Provider against third-party claims relating to the Client's business operations. Neither party shall be required to provide evidence of actual loss before seeking indemnification.

11. TERMINATION
Either party may terminate this Agreement by providing 15 days' written notice. The Client may terminate immediately if the Service Provider fails to meet any contractual obligation. The Service Provider may terminate immediately without prior notice if the Client delays any payment. Upon termination, the Service Provider shall retain all advance payments received, regardless of the amount of work completed. Service Provider shall transfer completed project files within 90 days after termination.

12. FORCE MAJEURE
Neither party shall be held responsible for delays caused by circumstances beyond reasonable control, including natural disasters, political instability, internet outages, cyberattacks, or government restrictions. No party shall be entitled to terminate this Agreement due to a force majeure event.

13. DISPUTE RESOLUTION
If mutual negotiation fails within 30 days, the dispute shall be referred to final and binding arbitration. The arbitration venue shall be determined by the Service Provider.

14. GOVERNING LAW
This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Bangladesh; the courts of Dhaka shall have exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes arising under this Agreement.

15. AMENDMENTS
An amendment shall become effective upon approval by either party's authorized representative. Email communications between the parties may also be treated as legally binding amendments.

16. ENTIRE AGREEMENT
This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between the parties and supersedes previous verbal or written agreements. Invalidity of one provision shall not affect remaining provisions.

17. SIGNATURES
Executed by authorized representatives of Nexora Digital Solutions Ltd. (Mr. Rahman Ahmed) and ByteCraft Technologies Ltd. (Mr. Tanvir Hasan), with two witnesses.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-002: Contracts must clearly define scope, deliverables, deadlines, acceptance criteria, and change-request procedures. Undefined or unlimited service obligations are unacceptable without specific Legal approval.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Define formal UAT acceptance criteria (15 business days) and written mutually signed Change Order procedure for any out-of-scope requests.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-003: Preferred payment structure is 30% advance, 40% upon milestone completion, and 30% after final acceptance (alternative schedules require Finance approval). Contracts must clearly define taxes, refunds, and reasonable late-payment conditions.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Milestone payment schedule: 30% advance, 40% upon milestone completion, and 30% after written final acceptance; late fee capped at 1% per month.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-005: Contracts must provide clear termination rights, 15-30 days preferred cure period for remediable breaches, and must address outstanding payments, refunds of unearned advances, completed work, and return of company property.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Provide a 15-30 day written cure period before termination for payment delay, and require pro-rata refund of unearned advance payments upon termination.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-006: Preferred aggregate liability cap is the total contract value (BDT 12,00,000), and clauses must consistently define direct/indirect losses, IP infringement, confidentiality breaches, and data security incidents.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Set Service Provider aggregate liability cap to 100% of total contract value (BDT 12,00,000), with uncapped liability for gross negligence, IP infringement, or confidentiality/data breaches.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-007: Preferred confidentiality survival is 3 years after termination. Contracts must mandate security obligations, breach incident reporting, return/deletion of data, subcontractor accountability, and Legal + Security review for personal data sharing.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Extend confidentiality survival to 3 years post-termination, hold Service Provider liable for personnel/subcontractor breaches, mandate 48-hour breach notification, and require prior written approval for third-party data sharing.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-008: Software contracts must define newly created IP, pre-existing IP, source code delivery, third-party/open-source dependencies, and commercial reuse permissions. Nexora requires exclusive ownership of commissioned deliverables without unapproved vendor commercial reuse.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Assign exclusive IP of commissioned deliverables (including source code) to Client upon milestone/final payment and prohibit commercial reuse of Client-specific deliverables without prior written Legal approval.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-009: Preferred software defect correction/warranty period is 60 days after final acceptance (exceptions require departmental and Legal approval).
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Extend free defect correction warranty period to 60 days after written final acceptance.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-011: Material assignment or subcontracting requires prior written company approval and must preserve confidentiality, security, quality, and accountability.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Require prior written Client consent for any subcontracting and maintain full prime-contractor liability for sub-processor actions.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-012: Contracts must explicitly allocate responsibility for applicable taxes, VAT, withholding (AIT), invoicing, and financial documentation.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Add explicit VAT, AIT/tax withholding, and Mushak-compliant invoicing clause.

playbook_rules.rule_description: Nexora Playbook NEX-CP-001 Rule CP-013: Preferred governing law is Bangladesh law with balanced dispute negotiation, formal notice, and fair arbitration/court venue without waiving mandatory statutory rights.
playbook_rules.suggested_redline: Seat arbitration mutually in Dhaka under the Arbitration Act, 2001 rather than unilateral Service Provider venue selection.

cases.notes: Real 5-page English Software Agreement (SDA-2026-011) audited against both Bangladesh Law and the real Nexora Corporate Contract Governance Playbook (NEX-CP-001).

cases.contract_title: Nexora-ByteCraft Cloud SaaS Subscription and Services Agreement (Compliant Baseline)
cases.contract_text:
CLOUD SAAS SUBSCRIPTION AND SERVICES AGREEMENT

1. PARTIES AND SCOPE
This Agreement is made between Nexora Digital Solutions Ltd (Vendor) and ByteCraft Ltd (Client) for subscription to the Vendor's cloud-based inventory management SaaS platform, including implementation and support services.

2. TERM
The initial term is twenty-four (24) months from the Effective Date. Renewal requires mutual written consent of both parties.

3. FEES AND ADVANCE PAYMENT
Client shall pay BDT 40,000 per month, due within thirty (30) days of invoice. An advance payment of two (2) months' fees is collected at execution. Any advance payment covering unperformed services shall be refunded proportionally to the Client upon termination, in accordance with Sections 64 and 65 of the Contract Act, 1872.

4. IMPLEMENTATION AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING
The Vendor shall complete implementation within forty-five (45) days. The Client has a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) window of fifteen (15) days and shall issue a rejection notice within five (5) business days of each defect report. The Vendor has a remedy period of ten (10) business days per rejected deliverable.

5. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
All custom source code and deliverables developed specifically for the Client are assigned to the Client, which becomes the first owner of copyright under the Copyright Act, 2023. The Vendor retains ownership of its underlying platform and grants the Client a non-exclusive licence for the term.

6. OPEN SOURCE COMPONENTS
The Vendor warrants that deliverables contain no copyleft (GPL) contamination and shall disclose all open-source components with licences. The Vendor shall indemnify the Client against third-party claims arising from undisclosed open-source usage.

7. DATA PROTECTION AND BREACH NOTICE
The Vendor shall notify the Client within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware of any personal data breach affecting platform data, consistent with the obligations of the Personal Data Protection Act, 2026, and shall cooperate in remediation.

8. MUTUAL INDEMNITY
The Vendor shall indemnify and hold harmless the Client against third-party patent or copyright infringement claims arising from the deliverables. The Client shall indemnify the Vendor against claims arising from data the Client supplies to the platform.

9. CONFIDENTIALITY
Each party shall keep the other's confidential information secret during the term and for three (3) years after termination.

10. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
Each party's aggregate liability is capped at the total fees paid in the preceding twelve (12) months. This cap does not apply to wilful misconduct or breach of confidentiality.

11. TERMINATION
Either party may terminate for convenience with sixty (60) days written notice. Upon termination the Vendor shall refund any unearned advance payment and the Client shall pay fees accrued to the effective date.

12. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
This Agreement is governed by the laws of Bangladesh. Disputes shall be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 2001, seated in Dhaka, before a sole arbitrator.

SIGNED for and on behalf of the parties hereto.
cases.notes: Compliant full-contract baseline (false-positive test): all TECH_SAAS mandatory provisions present; 12-month liability cap and 60-day termination are lawful commercial terms that must NOT be flagged HIGH. Exercises full segmentation + coverage-fill + synthesis path.

cases.contract_title: Delta-Meridian Industrial Equipment Supply and Installation Contract (Statutory Traps)
cases.contract_text:
INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT SUPPLY AND INSTALLATION CONTRACT

1. PARTIES AND SCOPE
Delta Engineering Works Ltd (Supplier) shall supply, install and commission three industrial boilers for Meridian Textiles Mills Ltd (Buyer) at the Buyer's Gazipur plant, for a total contract value of BDT 2,40,00,000.

2. DELIVERY SCHEDULE
Delivery and installation shall be completed within one hundred eighty (180) days of the Effective Date, in the milestones stated in Schedule A.

3. INSPECTION, REJECTION AND REFUND
The Buyer shall inspect goods within fourteen (14) days of each delivery and may issue a rejection notice for defective goods within that window. The Supplier shall refund the advance payment attributable to rejected goods within fifteen (15) days, consistent with the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 and Section 65 of the Contract Act, 1872.

4. LIQUIDATED DAMAGES
If the Supplier fails to meet any milestone, the Supplier shall pay the Buyer liquidated damages at five percent (5%) of the total contract value per day of delay, with no ceiling on the aggregate amount payable.

5. FORCE MAJEURE
Neither party is liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control; the affected milestone shall be extended for the duration of such event upon prompt notice.

6. NON-COMPETE
The Supplier shall not, for a period of three (3) years after completion or termination of this Contract, directly or indirectly supply, install or service industrial boilers to any textile mill operating in Bangladesh.

7. ADVANCE PAYMENT
The Buyer shall pay an advance of twenty percent (20%) on signing, adjusted against milestones; any advance relating to deliveries not commenced shall be refunded on termination.

8. TERMINATION
The Buyer may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days written notice, paying only for work performed; termination for material breach is effective on notice.

9. WARRANTY
The Supplier warrants the equipment against defects for twelve (12) months from commissioning and shall repair or replace defective parts at its own cost.

10. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
This Contract is governed by the laws of Bangladesh. Disputes shall be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 2001, seated in Dhaka.

SIGNED for and on behalf of the parties hereto.

expected_violations.rationale: Uncapped 5%/day LD on total contract value is a penal bond under s.74; Bangladesh courts treat wildly disproportionate LD as unenforceable beyond reasonable compensation (s.73).
3-year post-termination industry-wide non-compete is void ab initio under s.27 Contract Act, 1872 (restraint of lawful trade).

cases.notes: Full-length HIGH baseline for PROCUREMENT_SUPPLY: two defensible statutory traps (s.74 uncapped 5%/day LD, s.27 post-termination non-compete). Inspection/refund and arbitration clauses present so missing-provision gold stays empty.

cases.contract_title: GrandTech Permanent Employment Agreement (Compliant Baseline)
cases.contract_text:
EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT (PERMANENT APPOINTMENT)

1. PARTIES AND APPOINTMENT
GrandTech Bangladesh Ltd (Employer) appoints Ms. Rehana Karim (Employee) to the position of Software Engineer on a permanent basis, reporting to the Head of Engineering.

2. PROBATION PERIOD
The Employee shall serve a probation period of six (6) months. Confirmation shall be issued in writing upon satisfactory completion.

3. REMUNERATION
The Employee's gross monthly salary is BDT 90,000, payable by the 7th day of each calendar month, subject to statutory deductions.

4. WORKING HOURS AND LEAVE
Working hours are eight (8) hours per day and forty-eight (48) hours per week in accordance with the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006. The Employee earns earned leave at one day per eighteen (18) days worked, and casual and sick leave as provided by the Labour Act.

5. TERMINATION NOTICE AND SEVERANCE
Either party may terminate this employment by one hundred twenty (120) days written notice or wages in lieu of notice, in line with Section 26 of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006. Termination by the Employer for misconduct shall follow a documented opportunity for the Employee to show cause before the Labour Court or the Employer's disciplinary process, as applicable.

6. PROVIDENT FUND AND GRATUITY
The Employee shall be enrolled in the Employer's approved provident fund. Gratuity shall be paid at thirty (30) days' wages for every completed year of service in accordance with Sections 27 and 28 of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, together with all terminal benefits.

7. CONFIDENTIALITY AND RESTRAINT OF TRADE
During employment the Employee shall not, without written consent, engage in any competing business or accept conflicting engagements. The parties acknowledge that any restraint of trade extending beyond the employment term is void under Section 27 of the Contract Act, 1872; post-employment obligations are therefore limited to confidentiality of the Employer's genuine trade secrets under this Agreement's confidentiality terms.

8. RETURN OF PROPERTY
Upon separation the Employee shall return all Employer property, credentials and data in the Employee's possession.

9. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTES
This Agreement is governed by the laws of Bangladesh. Employment disputes shall be raised before the competent Labour Court, Dhaka.

SIGNED for and on behalf of the parties hereto.
cases.notes: Compliant employment baseline: 120-day notice per Labour Act s.26, gratuity/PF per ss.27-28, restraint confined to employment term with express s.27 acknowledgement (post-employment non-compete is void; only trade-secret confidentiality survives). Must NOT be flagged HIGH.

cases.contract_title: Harbour-Dhaka Traders Commercial Lease, 11 Months (Compliant Baseline)
cases.contract_text:
COMMERCIAL PREMISES LEASE AGREEMENT (ELEVEN MONTHS)

1. PARTIES AND PREMISES
Harbour Properties Ltd (Landlord) leases office space measuring 2,400 sq. ft. at House 12, Road 5, Gulshan-2, Dhaka (Premises) to Dhaka Traders Ltd (Tenant).

2. TERM
The lease term is eleven (11) months, commencing 01 January 2027 and ending 30 November 2027, unless terminated earlier under Clause 8.

3. RENT
Monthly rent is BDT 1,20,000 payable by the 5th day of each month. No escalation applies within the term.

4. SECURITY DEPOSIT
The Tenant has paid a security deposit of three (3) months' rent. The Landlord shall refund the security deposit within thirty (30) days of handover, after itemized deductions only for actual unpaid rent or documented damage beyond fair wear and tear. Deductions shall be supported by invoices or a joint inspection report.

5. STAMP DUTY AND REGISTRATION
This lease is executed on non-judicial stamp paper of the requisite value under the Stamp Act, 1899. The parties shall present this lease for registration at the sub-registry office under the Registration Act, 1908, so that it remains admissible in evidence, notwithstanding the term being under one year.

6. MAINTENANCE AND UTILITIES
The Landlord maintains structure and common services; the Tenant pays utilities and keeps the Premises in good order.

7. USE OF PREMISES
The Premises shall be used solely as a trading office. No hazardous or unlawful activity is permitted.

8. TERMINATION
Either party may terminate by sixty (60) days written notice. Early termination by the Tenant forfeits no deposit beyond Clause 4 deductions.

9. DISPUTE RESOLUTION
Disputes shall first be settled by negotiation, failing which by arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 2001, seated in Dhaka. Governing law is Bangladesh.

SIGNED for and on behalf of the parties hereto.
cases.notes: Compliant lease baseline: 11-month term, deposit refund with itemized deductions (no forfeiture), stamp duty + sub-registry registration clause. Must NOT be flagged HIGH.
